production.promotion_candidate_note_2026-08-28: The first promotion attempt for this release FAILED at the guard and deployed nothing (run 33189594086 was cancelled; before it, run 33188594374 conclusion=failure at step 3). Recorded because the cause is a standing trap rather than a one-off: deploy-production may only be dispatched from refs/heads/main and requires confirm_sha == github.sha, so it can ONLY ever deploy main's tip. A candidate had been staged and gated at 6731b585, and five further PRs were then merged to main, which silently made that candidate un-promotable. The fix was to stage main's new tip (cc07529c) and take the SHA and digest from that ONE staging run, which is what deploy-production's own error text prescribes. Freeze-then-merge is the ordering error to avoid; promote before merging further, or stage after.
production.environment_gate_note_2026-08-28: Five approval attempts on this promotion did not register. Cause, found by the owner: the production environment had 'Prevent self-review' enabled, and the owner is both the sole required reviewer and -- because dispatches from this lane run under the owner's identity -- the triggering actor. Turning it off did NOT release the already-queued deployment: GitHub evaluates environment protection rules when the deployment is created, so run 33189594086 stayed pending and had to be cancelled and re-dispatched as 33190886988, which then approved normally. Two consequences worth carrying: a protection-rule change needs a FRESH run to take effect, and 'Prevent self-review' is now OFF on the production environment -- it was providing no separation of duties with a single reviewer, but it is a control that is no longer there.
